newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs close sharply up on power rate rumors.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs close sharply up on power rate rumors.

text.p: Brazilian stocks closed up a strong 2.2 percent higher in hefty trade, led by soaring electricity stocks which jumped on rumors the government will sharply raise power rates, brokers said.
"There were rumors about rates and that set off electrical stocks. The rest of the market followed," one dealer told Reuters.
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa index of 49 most-traded stocks surged 1,495 points to close at 69,471 points on volume of 530 million reais.
The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index of nine most-liquid power shares rose 3.61 percent to close at 1,860 points on unconfirmed rumors Brasilia would authorize a hefty rate hike, brokers said.
Among leading power shares, Minas Gerais state-owned Cemig's preferred soared 9.55 percent to 36.70 reais, and federally owned Eletrobras' preferred surged 3.93 percent to 369.99 reais.
State oil firm Petrobras preferred piggy-backed on the power shares rise, climbing 4.07 percent to end at 153.50 reais.

Brokers said the wider bolsa also was heartened by news the government will indeed study ways to exempt stock trade from the new 0.2-percent CPMF check tax, which many fear will drive business away from local financial markets.
Experts contend average daily market volume could fall as much as 30 percent if stock transactions were subject to the levy, due to take effect January 23.
Bolsa benchmark Telebras preferred ended up 1.76 percent to end at 81.10 reais while its voting common share surged 3.51 percent to end at 73.70 reais.
"Telebras common has been rising because its price has been lagging," a broker said.
Despite the rise among top blue chips, state mining giant Cia Vale do Rio Doce's preferred share bucked the rising trend to end down 0.94 percent at 21.00 reais.
